newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's ruling party wins gubernatorial election.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's ruling party wins gubernatorial election.

text.p: Mexican election authorities on Friday confirmed that the ruling party candidate had won the governor's race in Campeche state, rejecting opposition parties' claims of fraud.

Antonio Gonzalez Curi of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) was declared the winner of the July 6 vote, although one opposition party filed a formal protest saying the PRI had falsified enough ballots to swing the election.
By confirming the PRI as the winner, the State Electoral Commission rejected 17 fraud claims made by the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).

Opposition parties made historic gains nationwide in the July 6 elections, which were touted as unusually fair and clean by election observers. For the first time ever, the PRI lost its majority in the lower house of Congress.
But the PRD claimed the PRI was up to its old tricks in Campeche, a sparsely populated state on the Yucatan peninsula.
The PRI has ruled Mexico for 68 years through a combination of patronage, populism and fraud.

Losing PRD candidate Layda Sansores immediately called on party rank and file to protest against the ruling with a campaign of civil disobedience. The smaller Labour Party (PT) said it would join the protests.
"We won't let the will of the people be played with," Sansores told Reuters. "We will continue with demonstrations of civil resistance because of this horrible fraud that was consummated today."
The PRI's Gonzalez outpolled Sansores by 15,351 votes, taking 108,249 votes to Sansores' 92,898.
But the PRD said the PRI had falsified 24,000 ballots and displayed purported copies of some at a July 22 news conference. The PRD also said the PRI's campaign spending surpassed legal limits.
